name: Tribute Taxes
overview: Scripture reveals that tribute taxes were a common practice among conquered peoples, as seen when the Canaanites dwelt among the Israelites and served under tribute (Joshua 16:10; Judges 1:30). In the New Testament, tribute money is highlighted in the context of Jesus' ministry, where tax collectors approached Peter about the payment of tribute, illustrating the ongoing obligation under Roman rule (Matthew 17:24). The decree from Caesar Augustus mandating taxation across the world (Luke 2:1) further underscores the historical reality of tribute taxes during biblical times.
